title: K-injective normalization and derived adjunction at an identity open locus
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. All schemes are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible commutative condensed coefficient [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Use the small pro-etale sites in the coefficient universe, the internal module categories $\Mod_{\Lambda_T}$, and the specified module pullback/direct-image adjunctions $f^*\dashv f_*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback, def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]. Their pullbacks are exact [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main]. Let $h:D\to Z$, let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ be a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and specify $h^{-1}(U)\cong U$ over $U$, with resulting open inclusion $i:U\hookrightarrow D$ and $hi=j$. No properness or density is assumed. Write $c_h:j^*h_*\cong i^*$ for the sectionwise comparison whose value at every pro-etale $T\to U$ is the identity on $M(T\to U\xrightarrow{i}D)$. Write $a_h:i^*h^*\cong j^*$ for the inverse of the composition comparison [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] for $hi=j$, using the canonical identity-pullback identification.

Assume the underived comparisons respect adjuncts in the precise sense that for every $t:h^*M\to N$ one has $c_{h,N}\circ j^*(t^\sharp)=i^*(t)\circ a_{h,M}^{-1}$, where $t^\sharp$ is the adjunct for the specified adjunction. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$, the total derived functors and their canonical adjunction $h^*\dashv Rh_*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Here an exact pullback denotes its termwise derived functor, and $a_h$ also denotes its termwise derived comparison.

Let $r_h:j^*Rh_*\cong i^*$ be the canonical natural restriction isomorphism of [lem-sfb-identity-open-derived-restriction] for $(Z',j')=(D,i)$; its hypotheses $hi=j$ and $h^{-1}(j(U))=i(U)$ hold by the specified identification. It has the following resolution normalization. For every K-injective resolution $P\to I$ on the small ringed-site module model [def-pur-kinjective-complex, lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport], it is represented by $c_{h,I}:j^*h_*I\cong i^*I$, followed by the inverse of the restricted resolution quasi-isomorphism identifying $i^*I$ with $i^*P$. The exact internal-to-sectionwise equivalence preserves K-injectivity, and the restriction $i^*I$ is K-injective. No image of $I$ under any additional non-open pullback is assumed K-injective.

Write $Q$ for localization of complexes and $\gamma_{h,P}:Q(h_*P)\to Rh_*(QP)$ for the right-derived comparison unit [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. The normalization satisfies
$$r_{h,QP}\circ j^*(\gamma_{h,P})=Q(c_{h,P}),$$
using the canonical exact-functor localization identifications. In particular $j^*Rh_*$, with this localized comparison unit, is a total right derived functor of $j^*h_*$. For the actual derived adjunction unit $\eta_h$ and counit $\varepsilon_h$, the following equalities hold for every $A\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Z})$ and $K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_D})$:
$$r_{h,h^*A}\circ j^*(\eta_{h,A})=a_{h,A}^{-1},\qquad i^*(\varepsilon_{h,K})=r_{h,K}\circ a_{h,Rh_*K}.$$
These equalities are natural in $A,K$ and use the specified derived adjunction, rather than an independently chosen adjunction on isomorphic functors.
